column1: # Fukuoka MQ Challenge: every recorded solve of types II, III, V and VI.
# THESE ARE PUBLISHED RESULTS, NOT INSTANCES. No challenge coefficient file and
# no answer vector is committed here; the challenge data carries no licence
# (see docs/research/fukuoka-mq.md section 3). Each row points at the page it
# was read from, which is also where that solve's answer vector can be fetched.
# Source of record: the challenge's own "full list of all submission details",
#   sha256 of the HTML as fetched: see docs/research/fukuoka-mq.md section 0
# plus, per row, the linked per-submission page named in the `details` column,
# The hall of fame on the front page shows only the five highest positions per
# type; this file is the complete list. Two of the site's own rules make it an
# UNDERCOUNT of what has been solved rather than a census:
#   Rule 2 - for a given n only the first five solves are recorded;
#   Rule 3 - a participant may record at most one solve per n.
# So the absence of a row for an (n, seed) pair is not evidence that the pair
#   type                    II, III, V or VI as the site labels it. Types II and
#                           III are the encryption families (m = 2n); V and VI
#                           are the signature families (n = floor(1.5 m)).
#   n, m                    variables and polynomials, as the detail page prints
#                           them. The site indexes types II/III by n and types
#   date                    submission date, ISO 8601, from the detail page.
#   figure_kind             WHAT runtime_seconds measures. The site mixes three
#                           conventions and does not flag the difference:
#                             per-subsystem-cpu    CPU seconds for ONE subsystem
#                             per-subsystem-wall   wall clock for ONE subsystem
#                           A per-subsystem figure is not comparable with a
#                           total and must never be quoted as one.
#   runtime_seconds         the `Running Time` figure converted to seconds.
#   phases_seconds          sum of the per-phase times the `Notes` field
#                           Recorded so the total can be checked against its own
#   peak_gb, peak_metric    peak memory and WHICH metric, where published. Only
#                           two rows have one, and they use different metrics
#                           (VmHWM and VmPeak), which are not the same number.
#   subsystems              number of subsystems solved before a solution was
#                           found, for the hybrid attacks that report it.
#   avg_subsystem_seconds   average time per subsystem, as reported.
#   processes               simultaneous processes, where the notes state it
#                           AND the three figures reconcile. Deliberately left
#                           `-` on three rows that state a count and an average
#                           but whose totals do not follow from them: type VI
#                           the two 2025 type VI rows (implying 7.6-way and
#   answer_published        whether the detail page prints the answer vector.
#   runtime_printed         the `Running Time` field verbatim, so the conversion
#                           in runtime_seconds can be rechecked by eye.
# Nothing in this file was measured, re-run or estimated here. Every figure is
# transcribed from the page named in its `details` column.
